original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Decide the open length-7 slice of PR #2116's formal F2[A4] four-role target diag([a],[b],[c],[d]) (240 rank-one paid factors D_N(g), g in {a,b}, four roles, no workspace, every formal coefficient): exact minimum 7 or 8.
scope_change_reason: The card asks broadly whether a nonabelian register model escapes the three-register obstruction; PR #2116 instantiated it as this A4 four-role target and left length 7 open. This package closes that one named slice (no other groups, targets, role counts or census extension), because a 7-word would have been the first sub-direct cross-role saving in the formal four-role finite-group family and an exact 8 closes the model on four roles.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the bit-mechanisms track: it decides that this nonabelian formal register endpoint has no paid-call saving (exact minimum equals the direct 8), so it gives no reason to price a native conversion of A4 group-algebra calls toward the bit primitive. It changes no selected supplier or kappa.
stop_rule: Submission rule committed before searching: a verified 7-word is submitted; an exact 8 is submitted only with a written structural lemma beyond the C3 determinant screen, otherwise nothing is posted. Stop with no PR if the primary join exceeds ~15 min wall or 1.5 GB RSS, or if the two joins disagree unresolved by the experiment deadline.
evidence: Written proof: C3 determinant (n_a = n_b mod 3) plus a radical-rank lemma (n_a >= 3 and n_b >= 3) exclude length 7 and lengths <= 5. Two exhaustive C joins, separately implemented in the same AI-assisted session (different state representation, multiplication side, enumerated end and hash) each expand all 6,655,830 minimal-length-3 classes against all 6,697,991 distinct products of length <= 3 (1,597,399,200 lookups each) and find no word of length <= 7, which also excludes length 6. The direct 8-word replays exactly on all 48 basis inputs. Controls: omissions, label mutation, three-output 6-words, planted 7-words, numeric checks of every lemma step. Verifier: research/a4-seven-call-radical-rank/verify.py, PASS_A4_FOUR_ROLE_EXACT_MINIMUM_EIGHT.
author: Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar)
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) in derivation, both C joins, the Python verifier and writing; reviewed by four independent AI review passes in the same loop; no independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can the length-6 case (n_a,n_b)=(3,3) be excluded by a written argument rather than exhaustive search?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would make the exact minimum a fully written theorem, reusable for role counts or targets where exhaustive search is infeasible.
open_questions.first_step: At (3,3) both step-5 identities are tight rank-3 decompositions with F2-rational columns aug(C_k)^-1 x_k; look for an incompatibility between the a-base and b-base decompositions or at the J^2 layer.

open_questions.question: Does the radical-rank label-count bound extend to G = P x| H with P a normal 2-group and H of odd order (for example SL2(F3) = Q8 x| C3)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would replace finite censuses by uniform per-label floors for nonabelian register models.
open_questions.first_step: State the lemma with S = F2[H] and an H-equivariant functional mu on the Frattini quotient of P, then test it against the existing SL2(F3) census of PR #2010 (research/sl2f3-conjugate-triple-seed592f).
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing for the formal statement; native conversion remains unpriced.
